title: Strings that exist to be compared, not read: assertions, ARIA, class names, date patterns, keys

census.why: The assertion arguments need their callee to be readable, which is an AST-tier fact.
JSX attributes carry their element and attribute name only at the AST tier.
Holds a translation KEY, whose value lives in another file.
The bundle holding the value that key points at.

No `.snap` reader, so the sweep surfaces its contents as `unclassified` and G2 refuses to pass. Correct: a snapshot mirrors production copy and has to be regenerated WITH it, never edited alongside it, and the engine cannot know that on its own.

expectations.why: This string exists to exercise quote escaping. Translate it and the test stays GREEN while testing nothing — the worst outcome available, because it is silent.
Same, one escape level deeper. The pair is what proves the classifier reads the assertion's callee rather than the string's shape.
Real French inside an assertion, so language detection alone would say translate. Position decides, not appearance.
A test NAME is prose a human reads in the runner output, and it sits two tokens from a fixture that must not move.
`polite` is a value from the ARIA specification, not an adverb. Translating it silently disables the live region for every screen-reader user.
Same vocabulary, and a word that exists in French with the same spelling.
Class names are a contract with the stylesheet. Two ordinary words separated by a space is exactly what a sentence looks like.

Locale-dependent and not translatable: `dd/MM/yyyy` and `MM/dd/yyyy` are the same pattern in two locales, so leaving it alone is as wrong as rewriting it and only a person knows which. Refusing is the answer.

The bug this case was written to catch. The quoted `'à'` made the whole pattern read as French, so it came back `translate` while its two short siblings in the same object were refused — three answers to one question. A model handed this renders the field letters and every date on the site breaks.
The third sibling, present so the object gives one consistent answer rather than three.
Genuine copy inside the same element as two ARIA values that must not move.
A key, not a phrase. Translating it detaches the component from its bundle and the UI renders the key itself.
The phrase that key points at. It is what should move, in a different file from the key that must not — which is the whole shape of the mistake.

knownGaps: The values in `src/locales/fr/common.json` come back do-not-translate/already-target-language on a fr→en run. The bundle is in the SOURCE language, so under `swap` it is exactly what should be rewritten; the reason given is the opposite of the situation. Asserted only as accounted-for here, because pinning the verdict would pin the confusion.

`'Enregistrement en cours'` lands on needs-judgment/no-rule while its ternary sibling `'Toutes les modifications sont enregistrées'` comes back translate. Same expression, two answers — the same inconsistency traps-persistence records in a switch.
